documents.title: AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
documents.evidence_scope: primary abstract reviewed; original summary, not implementation replication
documents.note: AlphaEvolve coordinates language-model code editing with evolutionary retention and evaluator feedback. The report describes applications to computing infrastructure and mathematical algorithms, including matrix multiplication. This is prior work on autonomous executable discovery loops. OPENEND cannot claim originality merely from combining generated programs with evaluation and evolution. Concrete comparisons require inspecting the search database and the task-specific evaluation setup beyond the abstract.

documents.title: Best Fit: tightest feasible remaining capacity
documents.evidence_scope: primary article abstract definition reviewed; host tie convention specified separately
documents.note: Best Fit puts the incoming item into the fullest bin in which it fits. On OPENEND feasible states this means minimizing residual capacity, with earliest-index tie breaking supplied by the host. Negative gap and negative remaining-space scores have this ranking. Positive item-to-remaining fraction also favors the smallest feasible remaining space for a fixed positive item. Surface algebraic changes need not create a new heuristic.

documents.title: First Fit: earliest feasible open bin
documents.evidence_scope: primary article abstract definition reviewed; no new theorem derived
documents.note: First Fit processes items in order and chooses the earliest bin that can accommodate each item. OPENEND's constant scoring policies implement this rule because all feasible scores tie and the host selects the earliest bin. A complicated expression that is identically constant on feasible states remains a rediscovery of this behavior.

documents.title: Evolution through Large Models
documents.evidence_scope: primary abstract reviewed; original summary, not a full-text snapshot
documents.note: ELM uses code language models as program mutation operators. Its reported MAP-Elites experiment produces Python controllers for simulated walking robots in Sodarace, then uses generated examples to train a conditional model. This is prior work connecting language-model variation with a quality-diversity archive. The abstract does not establish a comprehensive literature novelty verifier. OPENEND must distinguish any contribution from this established combination.

documents.title: Evolution of Heuristics: Towards Efficient Automatic Algorithm Design Using Large Language Model
documents.evidence_scope: primary abstract reviewed; reported performance not independently replicated
documents.note: EoH evolves heuristic descriptions together with executable implementations. Language models translate the descriptions into programs within an evolutionary search. The authors report improvements on combinatorial optimization tasks, including online bin packing. It is a relevant algorithm-design comparator for OPENEND. These abstract-level claims do not specify a faithful reproduction of its population, operators, prompts, data, or resource accounting; those require methods and implementation review.

documents.title: FunSearch: program database search mechanics
documents.evidence_scope: primary source code inspected and hash-pinned locally; limited primitives differentially tested
documents.note: FunSearch maintains islands of programs, clusters by per-test score signature, samples clusters with a changing temperature and favors shorter programs within a cluster. Weaker islands are reset from surviving founders. This is a search framework, not a bin-scoring formula. Corpus-relative sparsity weighting must be distinguished from these established diversity mechanisms. No result here reproduces native FunSearch performance.

documents.title: FunSearch published OR bin-packing piecewise residual scorer
documents.evidence_scope: primary released heuristic code read; not executed or independently benchmarked here
documents.note: The published OR heuristic maps residual capacity after placement into piecewise score bands. Small residuals receive high priority, while larger bands have nonmonotonic scores rather than a uniform best-fit ranking. Thresholds are expressed in raw item units. This is concrete prior art for thresholded residual bin scoring. Similarity of threshold mechanisms is a review lead, not proof of equivalence to a new policy.

documents.title: FunSearch published Weibull bin-packing aggregate and adjacent-score heuristic
documents.evidence_scope: primary released heuristic code read; no claimed transfer to OPENEND inputs
documents.note: The released Weibull heuristic combines squared remaining capacities, the maximum candidate-bin capacity, and powers of the item size. It changes score signs for nonexact fits and differences neighboring scores. This uses aggregate and cross-bin information unavailable to an independent scalar score based only on the current bin. Giving a restricted port the FunSearch name would hide a representation change.

documents.title: HARMONIC: item-size classes and separate active bins
documents.source_version: Lee and Lee, JACM 32(3), 1985, section 2; DOI 10.1145/3828.3833
documents.evidence_scope: primary paper section 2 inspected through a public PDF copy; original paraphrase only
documents.note: HARMONIC partitions normalized item sizes into reciprocal intervals and maintains an active bin for each class. Each arrival is assigned to its class and packed next-fit within that class. This is an established use of size thresholds and bin categories. OPENEND's host cannot generally express category-specific memory or open a fresh bin when another existing bin is feasible, so this mechanism is not an exact scalar-policy baseline under the current contract.

documents.title: Illuminating search spaces by mapping elites
documents.evidence_scope: primary abstract reviewed; original summary of the archive concept
documents.note: MAP-Elites organizes high-quality solutions along user-chosen descriptive dimensions instead of returning only one optimum. The resulting archive illustrates how performance relates to those dimensions and retains varied solutions. This supplies an established foundation for OPENEND's quality-diversity archive. Archive occupancy is a representation-dependent search measure; the abstract does not make it a certificate of novelty relative to all earlier literature.

documents.title: Next Fit and random-order bin-packing evaluation context
documents.source_version: Albers, Khan and Ladewig, MFCS 2020, section 1, DOI 10.4230/LIPIcs.MFCS.2020.7
documents.evidence_scope: primary paper introduction and algorithm definitions inspected; no claimed replication of bounds
documents.note: Next Fit uses the most recently opened bin and opens another when that bin cannot fit the item. Unlike OPENEND, it may leave feasible older bins unused. The paper distinguishes worst-case and random-order performance, reminding us that shuffling synthetic streams does not by itself establish a worst-case competitive guarantee. Best Fit and First Fit are separately defined in the same introduction.
